newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government denies Burma drug link.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government denies Burma drug link.

text.p: The Singapore government denied allegations of a link between investments by the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC) and a Burmese drug lord.
The allegations were contained in a programme aired by the Australian Special Broadcasting Service (SBS) in October. The allegations regarded the GIC's investment in the Myanmar Fund.

"GIC's investment in the Myanmar Fund is... completely open and above board. The Myanmar Fund's stakes in the two hotels and one company identified by the programme are straightforward investments in bona fide commercial projects," the Singapore government said in a statement issued on Saturday night.
The Singapore High Commission in Canberra wrote to SBS on October 26 saying the programme's "innuendos are preposterous".
The executive producer of the programme, Adrian Henning, told Reuters in Australia on Friday: "We stand by our story 100 percent."
